results.reasoning: Purpose is to encourage (not discourage) being active participant. Recorder is passive (not active). Express opinions (not lectures). → ①
Writing is invaluable (not worthless) tool. It is considerably more difficult (not easy). Discussions are disorganized (not organized). → ③
Be an active (not passive) participant. Note taking is manageable (not unmanageable). It can prepare (not hinder) you to speak. → ④
② useless contradicts context — writing is described positively as a tool for accomplishing tasks, so it should be invaluable. Others fit context.
④ drowsy is inappropriate — 'keep you active and drowsy' is contradictory. Should be alert. Others (participant, reacting, important) all fit.
③ marginally weakens the argument — the passage emphasizes difficulty, so 'considerably' (substantially) is needed, not 'marginally' (slightly).
'active _____, not a passive recorder' — the contrast demands participant. Recorder/emphasis/organization don't fit this slot.
'take notes and _____ what you want to say' — formulate (devise/organize thoughts) fits. Memorize/abandon/record are contextually weak.
'impose some _____ on the discussion' — organization is the natural collocate. Difficulty/lectures/emphasis don't combine with 'impose...on'.
invaluable = extremely valuable/precious. NOT valueless (in- is intensifier here). Worthless is opposite. Precious is synonym. → ③
formulate ≈ devise (both mean to carefully create/develop). Abandon is opposite; recall and postpone are unrelated. → ②
emphasis ≈ focus/stress. Reduction, criticism, distraction are all different concepts. Focus matches as synonym. → ④
active ↔ idle. Energetic/dynamic/engaged are all similar to active. Only idle means inactive/doing nothing. → ③
considerably ↔ slightly. Substantially/remarkably/significantly all mean 'a lot' like considerably. Only slightly means 'a little'. → ①
(A) Note taking = noun (written record). (B) Please note = verb (pay attention/observe). → (A) 메모/노트 — (B) 주목하다 → ②
Definition matches formulate: to create/prepare carefully with attention to details. Participate/emphasize/organize don't match. → ①
Parallel gerund structure: thinking, reacting, and ___ing. respond → responding.
Adverb needed to modify comparative 'more difficult'. considerable (adj) → considerably (adv).
'Unfortunately...when discussion begins, ____' — negative event follows. Pens and pencils go down = students stop writing notes. → ②
Third benefit of note taking (after staying active/alert and imposing organization). 'it can prepare you to speak' completes the series positively. → ③
